newsitem.title: UK: G7 summit to be held in Birmingham in 1998.
newsitem.headline: G7 summit to be held in Birmingham in 1998.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 22 (Reuter - Britain will host the 1998 Group of Seven (G7) summit in the central English city of Birmingham, Prime Minister John Major said on Saturday.

The G7 -- Britain, the United States, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan -- which has met since the 1970s, will also be joined by Russia for a meeting of the Group of Eight (G8), Major's office said.

Major made the announcement during a visit to Birmingham, where he was addressing a meeting of local government activists from the ruling Conservative Party ahead of an election he is expected to hold on May 1.
Britain will next year take over the G7 presidency from the United States, which will hold this year's summit in Denver in June. No dates were available for the Birmingham summit.
Previous British G7 summits have been held in London because of the large numbers of delegates and journalists attending.
"I am delighted that this time Birmingham will be able to show how well it can host major international conferences of this sort," Major said.
Major has been keen to move big international conferences out of London. Commonwealth heads of government meet in Edinburgh in October and next year's European Union summit will be held in Cardiff.
